items.title: Headlines for November 25, 2026 | Democracy Now!
items.excerpt: ## Army Publishes New Map Showing Lead Dust from Munitions Plant Detonation Could Spread to Missouri Nov 25, 2026 Iowa Governor Kim Reynolds has declared a disaster emergency in three counties, as the U.S. Army prepares to detonate nearly five tons of highly unstable lead-based explosives at an ammunition plant in southeastern Iowa today. Environmental groups are warning of an unfolding public health catastrophe, with a detonation scheduled for 9 a.m. Central Time that could spew toxic lead dust across communities, farmland and potentially into the Mississippi River. Officials have recommended that residents of Middletown, where the plant is located, and anyone within a five-mile cone southwest of the plant evacuate, while people living up to 20 miles away have been told to stay indoors with their windows closed. This is Sean Kaufman, a disaster preparedness official with the Department of Health and Human Services. > Sean Kaufman: “Individuals that are in that directly affected area — which, again, we will continuously get updates based on the weather — if they are women who are pregnant, children under the age of 6, or children in general, and individuals who may have chronic disease, you definitely want to be out of that area. I would evacuate that area.” The Army published an updated map estimating the lead plume could spread all the way to northern Missouri, more than 100 miles from ground zero. There is no safe level of exposure to lead, a neurotoxin that can cause permanent cognitive and behavioral harm. Ahead of today’s detonation, The New York Times published an investigation revealing the Army had initially hired a firm to turn the explosives into harmless waste, but then dropped the contract in favor of a so-called controlled blast. We’ll have the latest on this story after headlines. ## Gaza Health Officials Warn of Spread of Meningitis as Israel Continues to Violate Ceasefire Deal Nov 25, 2026 In Gaza, at least four Palestinians were killed this morning in an Israeli airstrike on an apartment building in the al-Shati refugee camp. The strike followed Israeli attacks that killed at least 10 Palestinians across Gaza on Tuesday, including a 30-year-old pregnant mother and Khaled Walid al-Jamal, a 13-year-old boy shot dead in northern Gaza City. Another Israeli airstrike killed a senior Hamas security official, along with his wife and their two teenage daughters. The relentless attacks came as Palestinians held funeral services in ... On Tuesday, Gaza’s Health Ministry declared an epidemic alert over a surge in meningitis, warning that hundreds of thousands of people are at risk of contracting the deadly condition. ## Yemen’s Houthis Strike Saudi Arabia’s Largest Refinery and Riyadh Skyscraper Nov 25, 2026 Saudi Arabia’s biggest oil refinery caught fire following an attack by Yemen’s Ansar Allah movement, known as the Houthis. Ras Tanura is one of the largest refining complexes and oil export terminals in the world, with a capacity of over a half-million barrels per day. It erupted in flames hours after a Houthi strike on Saudi Arabia’s main financial district in Riyadh Tuesday that injured 11 people. That attack damaged Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper, which is home to the kingdom’s sovereign wealth fund. The Saudi-backed coalition responded by attacking the Houthi-controlled port of Hodeidah, prompting Ansar Allah to threaten Jeddah and other ports on the Red Sea.

items.title: GDP (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 3rd Quarter 2026 | U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA)
items.excerpt: # GDP (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 3rd Quarter 2026 Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 4.3 percent in the third quarter of 2026 (July, August, and September), according to the second estimate released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). In the second quarter, real GDP increased 2.2 percent. The contributors to the increase in real GDP in the third quarter were increases in investment, consumer spending, and government spending that were partly offset by a decrease in exports. Imports, which are a subtraction in the calculation of GDP, increased. Real GDP was revised up 0.9 percentage point from the advance estimate, primarily reflecting upward revisions to investment and consumer spending. For more information, refer to the " Technical Notes" below. Compared to the second quarter, the acceleration in real GDP in the third quarter primarily reflected an acceleration in investment and an upturn in government spending that were partly offset by a downturn in exports. Imports increased more in the third quarter than in the second quarter. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers, the sum of consumer spending and gross private fixed investment, increased 5.8 percent in the third quarter, revised up 0.9 percentage point from the previous estimate. The price index for gross domestic purchases increased 2.7 percent in the third quarter, revised down 0.3 percentage point from the previous estimate. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index increased 2.1 percent, and the PCE price index, excluding food and energy increased 2.5 percent, both the same as previously estimated. Real gross domestic income (GDI) increased 4.4 percent in the third quarter, compared with an increase of 2.3 percent (revised) in the second quarter. The average of real GDP and real GDI also increased 4.4 percent, compared with an increase of 2.2 percent (revised).

items.title: Fed survey shows continued economic growth, sticky inflation in recent weeks By Reuters
items.excerpt: Nov 25 (Reuters) - Economic growth persisted at a "slight to moderate" pace across most of the US in recent weeks, while inflation remained sticky and employment levels rose, a Federal Reserve survey showed on Wednesday, two weeks before central bank policymakers decide whether to raise interest rates. "Prices increased moderately overall, as in the prior reporting period," the Fed said in its latest "Beige Book" report, a compendium of survey-based data and commentary from businesses compiled by its 12 regional banks to provide a read on economic conditions. "Contacts across a range of sectors reported sustained cost pressure from energy, transportation, health care, insurance, and tariff-related expenses." Still, input costs were outpacing selling price increases, suggesting growing pressure on corporate margins, the report said. "(C)ompetitive pressures and customer price sensitivity limited firms’ ability to fully pass through higher costs. Contacts expected both expenses and prices to continue rising in the coming months." ... The overall picture across the country was varied, with eight districts reporting growth and four reporting that activity was unchanged. Business investment — led by the artificial intelligence boom — remained strong, but consumer spending was flat as households were increasingly stretched and trading down.

items.excerpt: ## Judge halts order requiring Fulton County to turn over copies of 2020 ballots to Georgia election board A Fulton County judge today paused her own order from a day before that had required the county to hand over digital copies of its 2020 election records to the Georgia State Election Board. Superior Court Judge Kelly Lee Ellerbe halted the previous day’s order while the appeal from the county plays out. The move by Ellerbe, who issued a one-page ruling that did not elaborate on her reasoning, came hours before the 5 p.m. ET deadline to hand over records to the election board, which is controlled by allies of Trump. Fulton County, which is home to Atlanta and a large chunk of the state’s Democratic voters, has long been a target of Trump and his allies as they seek to find evidence to support their false claims of widespread voter fraud in the 2020 election won by former President Joe Biden. The records at the heart of the Georgia case are unredacted digital copies of 2020 election materials, the originals of which were seized from the county’s elections hub in January by the FBI in an unusual federal intervention into a state-run election. ... ## Trump administration blocked from carrying out the presidents’s renewed effort to limit birthright citizenship The Trump administration has been blocked from carrying out its executive order that would deny birthright citizenship to certain children of foreign government and international organization employees, as well as children born through surrogacy to non-U.S. citizens. U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper wrote that the Supreme Court made a very clear ruling on this issue, and he is following in its footsteps with this order. “The President cannot carve out new exceptions to birthright citizenship for children born within the United States and subject to its laws,” Cooper writes. “The Court will therefore certify a class consisting of children who are or will be unlawfully denied citizenship under the Order. And it will preliminarily enjoin the Government from enforcing the Order against members of that class.” “The Citizenship Clause promises citizenship to practically all children born in the United States. Earlier this year, the Supreme Court kept that promise by striking down EO1. This Court does so again today by enjoining EO2’s application as to the certified class.” A separate federal judge made a similar ruling in a separate case earlier this year.
